Our founders

A desire to see the community rise.

Anjuman-I-Islam was founded in 1874 by a small group of Muslims animated by a “desire to see the Musalmans rise higher in the moral, social and educational scale.”

In 1880 it presented a Memorandum to the Indian Education Commission emphasising vocational, industrial, commercial and agricultural education, physical education and education for girls. It started the first technical school for artisans in 1936 and its first girls’ school in 1939, and pioneered kindergarten, mid-day meals and subsidised fees for needy students.

Vision & mission

Our purpose

Vision

To enrich lives and develop model citizens through inclusive, globally competitive, quality education.

Mission

To create and nurture educational and social institutions with special focus on women and marginalized sections of society.

School values

To cultivate a dynamic learning community within our boarding school where every student is empowered to explore, discover and excel — fostering academic excellence, character development and global citizenship.

School mission

A transformative education beyond the classroom: a holistic environment that nurtures intellectual curiosity, creativity and personal growth, preparing students for success in higher education and beyond.

Goals

Six goals for the decade

  1. I

    Adequate infrastructure for all institutions

    by December 2027
  2. II

    Residential facility and new institutions — Schools, Health Care, Technical & Hospitality Management

    by December 2030
  3. III

    Build and enhance STEAM-based pedagogy in each institution

    by December 2027
  4. IV

    Obtain relevant accreditation for each institution

    by December 2027
  5. V

    Establish a Professional Development Centre (PDC)

    by December 2025
  6. VI

    Build capacity and competency of all professionals through a Performance Management System, including a Leadership Development Programme for all heads of institutions and CXO personnel

    ongoing

History

From 1874 to today

1874

Anjuman-I-Islam is founded in Mumbai by a small group of Muslims with a “desire to see the Musalmans rise higher in the moral, social and educational scale.”

1880

Presents a Memorandum to the Indian Education Commission urging vocational, industrial, commercial and agricultural education, physical education and education for girls.

1936

Starts the first technical school for artisans — the seed of today’s technical hub at the M.H. Saboo Siddik campus.

1939

Opens its first school for girls, which grows into the Saboo Baug girls’ education campus.

1946

Incorporated on 20 November as a not-for-profit company; also registered under the Maharashtra Public Trusts Act, 1950.

2020

The Panchgani school completes 100 years of imparting education — the Centenary celebration.

2024

Dr. Zahir Kazi, President since 2009, receives the Padma award. Robotics, Agriculture and Basic Aviation are added at Panchgani.

Leadership

Dr. Zahir Kazi

President, Anjuman-I-Islam since 2009 · Padma awardee

Dr. Zahir Kazi is a distinguished educationist and recipient of the Padma award, one of India’s highest civilian honours. Born in Ponda, Goa, he has served as President of Anjuman-I-Islam since 2009. Under his leadership Anjuman runs around 97 schools, colleges, hostels, orphanages and institutions across Maharashtra, serving over one lakh students, primarily from minority communities. Though a successful radiologist, he reduced his medical practice to devote more time to philanthropic work.
